_comment: RETIRING — EMPTY OF CONTENT since 2026-10-01 (bean `j7ql`, epic `7x5n`, issue #1770). Owner ruling 2026-10-01: large-datasets becomes a subgraph of cat-harness, DISSOLVED into cat-harness's concern groups rather than nested as a whole directory. Its skills are the `large-datasets` package in `cat-harness/skills/library/large-datasets/`, its five diagrams in `cat-harness/processes/`, its Zod schemas in `cat-harness/schemas/` (moving on to cat-harness-tools with the rest in S5), its code (`gen-id-lookup`, `bench-id-lookup`, the `lookup.js` client and its page) in `cat-harness-tools/`, and what was about one corpus went to that corpus's owner: `who-iris/sources/who-iris.json`, `who-iris/id-lookup/` (the generated index), `folio-assistant-sci/sources/lean-mathlib.json`. This declaration and the directory it sits in are kept, not deleted: retiring a declared instance is the OWNER's call (`deletion-requires-confirmation`), and what would go is listed on bean `j7ql`. Until then it declares no directory — declare only what exists (bean `dh4f`) — and needs only cat-harness, which now holds everything it held; it no longer needs folio-assistant-core. The previous comment, kept for the record: large-datasets, staged as a top-level named subgraph. Owner, 2026-09-20: 'maybe not core skill, sub-graph of skills to deal with "large data sets"'. It exists because a capability was missing from BOTH neighbours: `materialize-remote` (in folio-assist-core) answers 'may we take this, and what does holding it cost', and nothing answers the question before it -- how do you ENUMERATE a corpus, and how do you ask it for a SUBSET? Every source answers differently and none of it is guessable, so without a declared descriptor an agent asked for 'the WPRO style guides' must be told the API by a human every time. NOT in folio-assist-core, deliberately: core is the CONTENT layer, and this is about sources the instance will never hold. NOT in cat-harness: it is not about the harness either. It is the third thing, which is what earns it a subgraph rather than a directory inside one.
